extracted.intended_audience: authors and aspiring writers of cozy mystery novels (especially those blending subgenres)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing cozy mysteries and mixing in other genres (historical, paranormal, romance) while preserving cozy conventions and making the blended elements integral to plot and character. Focuses on what defines a cozy and how to adapt genre-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core cozy prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cozy mysteries are mysteries without on-the-page violence, physical intimacy or naughty words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remain true to the roots of cozy mysteries: avoid graphic/gory descriptions, explicit sex scenes, and obscene language on the page. This is a defining constraint when blending other genres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key cozy elements (what cozies should include)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond what they exclude, cozies typically include humor, quirky secondary characters, closeknit communities, and intrepid amateur sleuths who use their unique skills and an investigative team to solve murders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize these positive features—tone (humor), character types (quirky supporting cast), social setting (close-knit community), and protagonist role (amateur sleuth whose unique perspective/skills drive investigation). These elements help distinguish a cozy from other mystery forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical cozy authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: When combining historical fiction with a cozy, you must show the historical era through events, people, attire and language rather than just stating the date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid anachronisms (e.g., modern slang, contemporary cultural references). Ensure investigative methods reflect the era (e.g., fingerprinting not widely used in U.S. until 1900s, DNA testing not until 1980s, no social media research for 1930s settings). Use era-appropriate technology, social norms, and vocabulary to make the setting believable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paranormal cozy integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Paranormal elements must be more than window dressing; supernatural features should be used to help solve the mystery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test: 'If you can remove all of your paranormal elements from your story without hurting the plot, then you haven’t written a paranormal cozy mystery novel.' Make supernatural abilities/ghosts/talking animals functionally relevant to plot progression, clues, or resolution rather than merely decorative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romantic cozy (romcozy) integration
rubrics_metrics.description: In romantic cozies, the romance—usually involving the amateur sleuth—is combined with mystery; the romantic relationship should be important to the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sleuth often has a romantic interest who may be on the investigative team or in law enforcement. Indicate that the characters are destined for romance (fireworks or slow burn). Test: 'If the mystery and character conflicts remain intact without the romance, then you don’t have a romantic cozy mystery.' The romance should contribute to conflict and/or resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgenre-blending principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may mix other fiction genres (historical, paranormal, romance, steampunk, etc.) into cozy mysteries but must preserve cozy fundamentals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blending is encouraged as a way to expand the cozy subgenre, but maintain the cozy's core constraints and characteristics (tone, community, sleuth type, and content prohibitions). Ensure the blended elements are integral to plot/character rather than superficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amateur sleuth characterization and team dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Cozies often center on an intrepid amateur sleuth who leverages unique skills and an investigative team of secondary characters to solve murders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the sleuth's skills and the contributions of their informal team plausible and central to detection. Secondary characters should be quirky and contribute to both tone and plot (providing leads, motives, obstacles, or comic relief).
